section: Prologue: Mission Assignment at London MI6
description: On July 3, 1961, at the London MI6 headquarters, Section Chief Turner summoned four new agents to assign an urgent mission to retrieve stolen diplomatic documents from Frankfurt, introducing the background of Frankfurt Station Chief Brandt.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: A new story begins, wishing you a pleasant journey!

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: On the night of July 3, 1961, London was shrouded in damp, stifling heat. The investigators were spending their hard-earned vacation in their preferred ways, but the piercing ring of the telephone shattered the peace that should have belonged to a Sunday evening. "Hello, it's Turner. Looks like your leisurely Sunday is ending early—yes, no complaints, you're agents 'serving the country,' after all. Now listen, I need you to head to 54 Broadway, MI6 headquarters, immediately. Yes, put on your formal attire, and don't let me hear any nonsense like 'can it wait.' Click..." Willing or not, you arrived at 54 Broadway as scheduled and entered the familiar lobby, which seemed darker than usual on a Sunday night. The main entrance of the headquarters building faced a wooden screen, behind which were three old elevators that groaned and creaked. The guard in the duty room was dozing off, and the spokesperson on a Machavati tea advertisement on the glass window was wide-eyed, keeping watch for any uninvited guests on the guard's behalf. Turner's office was on the fourth floor; you'd better not keep him waiting.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew puts on his best clothes, tidies himself up, and maintains a full, optimistic attitude to meet his superior.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David looks around; it seems everyone is tired and worn out today. He wears a casual suit and heads to the fourth floor to see the boss; it would be even better if there were some unlucky souls to go up with him.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Adjusts his attire and steps forward to press the elevator button.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The four of you meet up. As classmates from the training course and colleagues working under Turner, you're already familiar and don't need much small talk. The elevator creaks and groans as it ascends, making one wonder where the damn funding is being spent.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Wearing a well-tailored three-piece suit, straightens his tie before entering and steps into the lobby calmly.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Shows great respect to his senior colleagues and is very excited about the task he is about to face!

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You arrive on the fourth floor. The usual office hours have passed, and the air carries a hint of desolation and tension. However, the Logistics Section office is still lit, clearly prepared for you.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David counts heads and enters the room third in line.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Walks straight to the office, stops at the door, and knocks lightly three times in a rhythmic manner.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: As the junior, how could Andrew be the first to enter the room! He respectfully follows behind, but his toes keep tapping the ground lightly.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Clears his throat and waits by the door for a response from inside.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Come in." A voice that is neither friendly nor hostile, difficult to gauge the emotion, responds to you.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Pushes the door open and stands to the left of the boss's desk.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Files in with the other colleagues, lining up in front of the boss's desk.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Good evening, lucky ones." Turner sits behind his desk, looking out the window at the blurred London skyline in the night, appearing utterly bored.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Invites his senior colleagues to enter first, takes responsibility for closing the door last, and then stands to the side.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Ready to say goodbye to craftwork and get down to real action?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I'm ready!"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Just looks at the boss, waiting for him to continue.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David first glances at the expressions of his other colleagues; seeing Andrew's eager, almost SpongeBob-chasing-jellyfish-like demeanor leaves him speechless. He nods restrainedly.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Been ready since the training ended."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Then pick up the first folder on your left on the table. Mission briefing."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew looks left and right. Is anyone going to take it? Is anyone going to take it? If no one does, I'll take it then.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Seeing you all so timid and nervous, Turner also puts away his joking demeanor.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Whether left or right, both are far from David. David doesn't move, letting the eager junior take it.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Turns his head to look at Andrew, who is closest to the desk, waiting for Andrew to reach out and take it.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Yay! Andrew quickly steps forward, grabs the folder from the table, and retreats while opening it. He takes out the mission briefing from the folder, suppresses the urge to read it aloud, and passes it around for everyone to see.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Waits for teammates to finish reading, takes the document, and memorizes it word by word.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: As you read the briefing, Turner took a sip of coffee and began speaking, "By the way, just like parents introducing distant cousins their children have never met before a long trip, I'll also introduce the few people mentioned here."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew listened intently; all this information was both fresh and useful, and they were going abroad! Yay!

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He paused slightly, then continued in that cadenced tone, "And then there's our good cousin, the American Central Intelligence Agency. They also have a station in Frankfurt. Recently, they've been a bit unhappy because of the Blake incident. They've demanded a suspension of all intelligence sharing with us and even started suspecting there might be a traitor within our ranks. Their message is simple: MI6 is full of leftists and traitors; we must clean house before cooperation can resume. You know, I don't need to tell you what the CIA is like. This time, they've come with a 'struggle behind enemy lines' plan and have put us in the cold."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Thinking of his pleasant experiences at MI6, Andrew found the CIA's baseless accusations baffling; it seemed completely unfounded.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David wasn't too concerned about his career, but when it came to cleaning house, he perked up. It seemed they weren't planning to clean him out yet, so he'd listen to what the boss had to say next.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Then, he deliberately加重ed his tone, raised his eyebrows, and glanced through the half-open curtains outside: "And as for the KGB—well, that's what you really need to be careful about. Regarding the KGB station in Frankfurt, we have substantial evidence, especially of them repeatedly intercepting and assassinating guests our cousins invited from Eastern Europe. You know what I mean? Although your first mission as rookies isn't noteworthy, it's routine to stay vigilant. Be especially wary of women who throw themselves at you..." He glanced at you all and shrugged, "Or men, perhaps."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew's face turned red, his heart pounding. So those rumors were true?

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David gave a strange look to the blushing Andrew.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison wasn't concerned about her career, nor was she interested in men; she just hoped this mission would be completed smoothly.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Finding a swallow in a tight ten-hour schedule is quite challenging."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Turner picked up the coffee on the table and savored it. Having spent some time with Turner, you knew this was the best time to ask any questions.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "If the CIA causes obstacles during this mission, how should we handle it?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "If you have no brains, you could beg the CIA for mercy. After all, why not? Our friends across the ocean always love playing the savior, right? If you think your career has reached its end, or if you feel MI6 hasn't lost enough face recently and needs this move to seal the coffin, go ahead. But if you have any ambition left, don't let the cousin meddle in the big brother's family affairs, understand?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "The briefing mentions civilian terrorist organizations. If we encounter obstruction from such groups, what actions are we authorized to take?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Why does a file from the archives require the four of us to fly to Frankfurt to retrieve it? Can't the local intelligence station spare someone to deliver a package?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "So, will there be overseas mission allowances for this task?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Quite bold to ask. David looked at his colleague; he thought one shouldn't question the boss's task arrangements.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "After the Blake defection case, MI6 increased security levels for all 'errand' tasks. And since the personnel relationship review related to Blake isn't finished yet, tasks have been piled onto new agents who joined after Blake's arrest—yes, that's your batch. None of you worked with Blake, so you're 'clean.'"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Yay! I'll keep the accounts clear and request a bit more funding when appropriate."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Are we getting weapons for this mission? At the very least, we need something to forcefully shut the CIA up."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Of course. Then there's your equipment. I think I don't need to say this, but I hope you haven't forgotten everything you learned at school. However, it's worth mentioning there are your favorite cyanide capsules. If anyone wants to visit Göring, I won't stop them."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: This is really good cooking material.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "But I think a courier mission doesn't require guns. You know how difficult it is to check firearms."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Let Meyer enjoy such delicacies alone." David browsed the list, happily noting that everyone had 3000 Marks.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I hope we never have to use that thing." Jotting down some key information.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "By the way, this safe house is confidential; only headquarters knows. Even the Frankfurt station isn't aware. Keep your mouths shut."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Yay! We'll complete the mission!"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Having the same luck as Turner is really unfortunate. David thought to himself, no more questions.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison had no more questions and glanced around at her teammates.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "When do we get the 3000 Marks?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Should we first contact Station Chief Brandt upon arrival, or head straight to the mission location?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "By the way, if you're brainless, you can also seek help from the CIA instead of coming to me when you encounter problems, just as I said earlier, if you think MI6 hasn't lost enough face recently."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David nodded thoughtfully.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "As you wish, I've said enough about Brandt just now."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: It seems the leadership believes Peter Brandt is trustworthy. After arriving in Frankfurt, we can approach him to learn more mission details. No further questions to ask, remaining silent.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Can we get the money now?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Go get it from logistics yourself. I haven't even received my salary this month."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Yay"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Turner sat back in his chair, the smile on his face gradually fading, replaced by a barely noticeable seriousness. He paused, leaned back in his chair, and his tone gradually cooled down: "Your mission may seem simple, but I hope you understand that the complexity of espionage work is never the mission itself, but how far you can go in this unknown gray area."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Yes, sir"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Yes, sir"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Yes, sir"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Yes, sir"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: ——Divider——

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David sized up this person, secretly comparing whose hair was redder. "We are deeply honored that the Consul General sent you to welcome us."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Thank you, we'll need your guidance here as well." Giving him a polite smile.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Thank you! It's wonderful to meet you!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He extended his hand, shaking hands with each of you. "I suppose the journey was comfortable enough? Business class service is at least better than the tea here." As he spoke, he gestured for you to follow him to the car parked nearby—bearing British diplomatic plates.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Pleased to meet you." Also showing a specially trained polite smile. "The weather in London is just too changeable; Frankfurt's sunshine is much brighter."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Yes, that's one good point. Welcome to Frankfurt, Germany's financial capital," he said, shaking his head slightly. "Maybe it's the financial capital, but I'd rather call it the 'concentration camp for British civil servants.'"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Walk around the car to check it out, then sit in the back seat.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Follow colleagues into the car one after another. Time waits for no one, better pay respects quickly and get to work.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You know, those of us sent here, aside from drinking barely passable beer, sit at the same table with Americans discussing 'how to protect Europe.'" He drew quotation marks in the air with his fingers, a smile full of sarcasm on his lips. "Of course, 'protect' means staring at a place on the map called the 'Fulda Gap,' and hoping the Soviets will give us weekends off and not disturb our tea time."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hah, protecting Europe. It's really just making the public believe they're protected, but we all know they're not."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: What is the Fulda Gap? Andrew could only scratch his head.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "The Soviets always have endless energy, and they don't attend church on weekends, let alone rest."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "How's the food?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "...The Russian and East German armies are just 200 kilometers away. To be honest, their tanks could reach the entrance of our Consulate General in three days. Sometimes I think we should really get a Consul General of French descent; they have more experience handling surrender matters."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Sounds like being stationed abroad really isn't a good choice...

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: How dare this guy even mock the Consul General? David raised an eyebrow internally.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Without you and your colleagues' hard work here, we'd be completely in the dark when we arrived."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Kicks Andrew under the table and strikes up a conversation with Jackson. "A weekend in Belgium wouldn't be bad either, the beach is a real lifesaver."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Compared to Belgium, I prefer the scenery of Sardinia and Sicily. The Mediterranean sun is as gentle yet fiery as the ladies there."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew, having been kicked, quiets down.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "That depends on which beach. I've been to Omaha Beach, it's eerie. Hard to imagine American soldiers charging machine guns there twenty years ago."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: His colleagues' experiences are so rich, their work skills so formidable... Andrew feels immense envy.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The American troops in Germany are all on drugs now, they don't even know which side they're on. During the last NATO exercise, American soldiers disbanded in the woods and went on a picnic with the female soldiers."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: It seems the Cold War front isn't all that oppressive and brutal, but full of life's laughter and joy. This firsthand experience was definitely worth coming for. "Female soldiers from which country?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Glances at Andrew. Why is this kid always so active on such topics?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I bet it definitely wasn't West German. Germans are a bit more reliable than Americans. They've killed tens of millions of Russians, and some former war criminals are still shining in the Ministry of Defense, though they're now busy cleaning themselves up."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew, having been glared at, lowers his head, no longer expecting an answer.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "After losing the war over a decade ago, because of all the crap they did—I mean, killing 6 million Jews—Germans were expelled from human society. Now they're split into two factions: a small group playing neo-Nazis, and the majority playing civilized anti-Nazis. Then the majority opposes the minority, so they can show they've reflected and can rejoin human society."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Ha, if the Soviets really attacked, those Yanks would probably all run away in under three hours."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Speaking of which, if you want to see the animal show of neo-Nazis, there's some organization called the 'Thule Tradition Association' making a big fuss these days. You could check it out..."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew looks up at Sister Alison. "Can we go see it?" Andrew seeks his teammates' opinions.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: @player2 "Hahaha, spot on!" Can't help but burst out laughing. "I say these Germans should all get a taste of the concentration camps. There are still neo-Nazi monkeys daring to strut around the streets these days?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Haha, if they go to the circus, it's better than clumsy dwarfs jumping through fire hoops." David chimes in. "The Thule Tradition Association has activities recently? It'd be better if they caused less trouble."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Perhaps there are other places we could ask Consul General Secretary Jackson to show us... though I know it's probably not very appropriate..."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Let's finish our primary duties first."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Schiller, we still have a mission. Another time when we're free on a business trip, we'll ask the consul secretary to show you Germany's special animal performances."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Yes, I understand."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: On the way to the consulate general, Jackson chatters incessantly, his mouth never stopping. From the taste of different brands of whiskey to the Partition of India, from Churchill's romantic affairs to the bestseller 'The Lost Victory'.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew listens with great interest, but he can't contribute much to the conversation and is always subject to speech control, so he just pricks up his ears.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: New character created and automatically bound: Lev Mikhailovich player5. I've recorded everything clearly, won't forget.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: After enduring an hour of relentless verbal bombardment, you finally arrive at the consulate general, 11 o'clock, on time. It's a three-story standalone building with light yellow paint on the exterior walls. Though clean and tidy, it appears somewhat shabby compared to the former glory of the British Empire. A British flag stands beside the main entrance, slightly worn by the gentle breeze, as if telling of the country's current situation: still dignified, but clearly not what it once was. A small garden surrounds the main building, the greenery neatly trimmed. A device with a tall chimney is particularly conspicuous in the garden.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: This guy's mouth has more rounds than a US Army magazine. David is glad to finally be free from the bombardment, squinting as he examines the main building. "What's that?" He points at the chimney device and asks the chatterbox.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Tall chimney! Has Andrew seen something similar before?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Jackson says with a smile, "That's our incinerator, specifically for disposing of expired documents. Every letter, every page of paper in the consulate general gets devoured into ashes by that thing at a certain point—a 'unique' security measure, you could say. You know, we can't let the Soviets reach too far." After saying this, he pushes open the car door and leads you towards the consulate's main entrance.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: This is where the work will be carried out next. Honestly, not bad. Andrew feels he'll come to like this place, leaving behind unforgettable memories here. Andrew looks around all the way, observing every thing and every person he encounters.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David nods in deep agreement. Confidentiality work must be done well.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: As he walked, he said, "To be honest, although this building is small, it's considered quite good for Frankfurt. After all, our Great Britain's current diplomatic budget..." He shrugged, his tone light with a hint of bitterness. "Let's just say it's enough to not lose face, but not enough to make us look too glorious. It perfectly matches our national situation—'knowing when to stop,' very British elegance."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew nodded.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: A slight nod, a basic confidentiality measure.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: He hadn't experienced the more illustrious days of the British Empire and accepted the current situation quite well.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Anyway, going to the Treasury for budget requests, you'd only be told 'the money has been spent where it matters most.'" David shared the sentiment with him.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Mr. Jackson's extensive knowledge and insights are truly impressive. Going out always brings new discoveries."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Make a Spot Hidden roll.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player3>'s Spot Hidden check result:

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Sometimes I even want to apply for the 'Red-Headed League.' Copying the Encyclopædia Britannica at least doesn't require using your brain."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You get out of the car. The warm Frankfurt sun shines on the small garden of the consulate, so peaceful it seems carefree. But Gray catches a faint glint coming from the direction of the garden.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hah, those Treasury bureaucrats are quite generous when it comes to their own perks. While in office, they help certain projects get extra funding; after retirement, they land lucrative positions on some advisory committee or at a bank."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s Spot Hidden check result:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: player5 is also pricked.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: If he were a fan of Conan Doyle, it would be better, at least不至于让大卫牧师搜肠刮肚地想话题.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Pretend to chat with someone, turn to look towards the garden, squinting slightly, trying to see the source of the glint.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Led by Jackson, you enter the main gate. A man slowly approaches from the garden direction. He is in his early sixties, with graying hair and an unremarkable face, looking like any ordinary elderly Western European man, with a camera hanging around his neck.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Brother Jackson, what kind of flowers are planted in your garden here? Could you introduce them to us?"

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s Photography check result:

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: That might be our Deputy Consul? Andrew boldly speculates.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Mountains and soil listen to your hopes; regardless of what karma and retribution, fate already slumbers in your palm.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Johnsen tries to identify what brand the camera is, but being too focused, he trips without noticing.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s Hard Dexterity check result:

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Although Andrew didn't notice anything unusual, he saw Johnsen suddenly about to kiss the ground at a weird angle.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Johnsen, how could you be so careless?" Steps forward quickly to support him.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Jackson quickly walks to the middle of your group and introduces, "Allow me to introduce, everyone, this is Deputy Consul Peter Brandt."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Hello, Deputy Consul!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Brandt steps forward, his smile radiating warmth. His face is undoubtedly the ideal type for intelligence work—ordinary to the point of being unremarkable, like some kind of calculated "average face."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "It's an honor to meet you, sir."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Welcome, welcome!" Brandt waves his hand, his voice carrying a hint of aged hoarseness but not lacking enthusiasm. "I heard you were coming, so I came out for a stroll,顺便随处拍点照片, a personal hobby."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Supported by Rabin, Johnsen steadies himself without kissing the ground. He straightens his clothes. "It's an honor to meet you."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "You truly are the gentle and refined English gentleman as described by the station chief," stepping forward to greet.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Enjoying life, enjoying living, truly wonderful. Andrew thought this was really a role model for his own life, but he strongly suspected Mr. Brandt must be hiding another side unknown to others; otherwise, how could he reach such a position?

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Was Brandt just taking our photo? David pondered.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You tacitly acknowledge each other's spy identities. He gently patted the camera hanging on his chest, smiled and said, "The lighting here is good, and the plants are full of life, although this city..." He looked up, his gaze towards the incinerator at the edge of the garden, and gave a slight shrug. "Frankfurt is quite livable, but if something really happens, I guess in three days we'd all have to learn how to plant potatoes with shovels, right?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Given current trends, it might be learning to grow corn," replying with a professional smile to joke.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "With you and our colleagues here, we believe it won't be that easy," continuing to maintain a polite smile.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "It seems the ability to learn and adapt is important no matter where you go," David also chimed in.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Planting potatoes in Frankfurt would be terrible; Andrew would rather plant them somewhere farther from the front lines. Thinking this, the work in Frankfurt didn't seem so great either. Andrew just smiled along.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I'm truly sorry to interrupt everyone's chat, but I suggest we save this discussion for afternoon tea, how about that? Let's prioritize your official business. I've already arranged for personnel to take you down to the vault on the underground level to get the documents. Strange, they should have been waiting for us on the first floor by now." Jackson checked his watch, looking around somewhat nervously.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Hmm? Faced with something unusual, David became alert.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hmm?" slightly frowning, feeling something was off, "Then let's hurry over quickly."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: On our own turf in Frankfurt, nothing should go wrong, Andrew thought.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Thank you for your trouble. Deputy Consul General, we'll excuse ourselves first," Alison decided to get the documents first before dealing with anything else.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Just then, the sound of leather shoes descending the stairs was heard. You watched as the guard, looking slightly embarrassed, hurried over. "Mr. Jackson, I went to the duty room on the second floor to find today's duty secretary, but he wasn't there. The keys were still hanging on the wall in the duty room. I waited a while, but he didn't return, so I took the keys and came here."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew scratched his head. This was too amateurish even for a semi-amateur like himself. How could they do the work in Frankfurt properly with people like this?

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The duty room being unmanned—is that normal?

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Let's hurry, Mr. Jackson. Is this situation common?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Mr. Jackson, I assume this isn't the norm for the Frankfurt station," still wearing a somewhat fake smile, but the voice had turned cold.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David looked at Rabin and Gray, noticing their expressions were also serious.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Upon hearing the guard's words, Jackson's expression quickly shifted from his usual professional smile to a wry one. His tone remained steady, even with a hint of humor: "Oh, wonderful. It seems this duty secretary has clearly found his 'time for afternoon tea.' That's the British attitude to life—tea is more important than God," he chuckled, though a trace of faint annoyance was audible in his lighthearted words. "I hope this won't affect things too much. My apologies."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "I think the priority now is to confirm the status of the vault," David mediated. "The vault has guards, I assume?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Then how about having the guard take you to get the documents? Please excuse me, I must take my leave for a moment to report the work situation to the Consul General."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "As long as it doesn't affect official business, it's fine. I hope we can get the documents smoothly later; maybe we can even find time to enjoy some afternoon tea ourselves."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Is this according to regulations?" Andrew picks a lucky teammate to ask.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Guard, please take us there at the fastest speed possible."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David also nodded seriously.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Preparing to jog along with the guard.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: If everyone is running, then Andrew will run too.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Wishing you success in your work." Brandt picked up his camera again, pondering, and gradually walked away.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Obviously not, but we don't have time to investigate these matters now," heading to the vault as quickly as possible.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You jog all the way to the vault.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Taking a deep look at Brandt's camera, then turning to follow the guard.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The vault door has two keyholes, spaced farther apart than a person's arm span, ensuring it requires two people turning simultaneously to open. The guard explains the confidentiality principle: one key is kept by the Security Department, the other by the duty secretary of the Consulate General. The two custodians rotate daily, and the rotation order is kept secret from each other to prevent collusion and unauthorized opening of the vault. Due to special circumstances, an exception is being made today. The guard asks for your help in turning the key on the other side.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew finds it absurd that the biggest flaw in the strictest regulations is the people who enforce them.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "The Security Department's key is always under supervision, right? I hope our security team hasn't gone for tea."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Give me the key, thank you." Andrew takes a key and goes to assist in opening the door.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Andrew and the guard turn the keys together, opening the door. The moment the door opens, a damp, musty smell mixed with the accumulated dust of ages hits you like a blow to the head, making you dizzy. Although the floor appears free of mold, clearly maintained regularly, the environment inside the warehouse is still unbearable. Thick mold patches on the walls are mottled like a post-war ruin, growing wantonly in every crevice they can inhabit, filling every inch of space with a "living" scent.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Ugh." Andrew fans the air in front of his nose repeatedly. "Speaking of which, this warehouse is so big. Do we know where to find the file?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Can paper documents really be stored in this environment without damage?

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David examines the floor, wanting to see if there are any fresh traces besides their own.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "You go get the file first. I think I left something behind." Professional sensitivity makes Lev feel something is off. He decides to go back and keep an eye on the secretary who claimed to report to Brandt and Brandt himself.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Alright, then we'll search here for the file first."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player3 Spot Hidden

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Is the cycle of fate a shackle, and will you now gamble on the untraceable? <player3>'s Spot Hidden check result: D100=12/25 Hard Success. Copying books was indeed useful. Trust my experience.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Guard, do you know where the file we're looking for is? Or do we need to randomly browse through the files here until we find what we want..."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David nods at Rabin, signaling him to be careful.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: It seems Andrew is too focused on being a chef, forgetting the most basic universal filing classification method. Hopefully, his teammates can remind him that GER.B.11451 represents Germany Section, B Series, File Number 11451.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David examines the traces, truly hoping the area around our file is still pristine.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Maybe we can only make Scottish haggis pudding for Turner when we get back.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Seeing everyone hesitating at the entrance of the file vault, Andrew hesitates too.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: David notices many scattered footprints on the floor, distributed throughout the vault without a clear pattern, likely left by secretaries coming in to access files. However, the frequency of a size 43 men's shoe print is much higher than other footprints.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Aren't we going in to find the file?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David mentally notes the shoe size and sole pattern. He heads towards the 11451 file, observing if this footprint extends near the file.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Observe the traces at the entrance, and while heading to the file location, look for any traces leading from the entrance to the vicinity.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: player5 goes back to find Jackson and Brandt, then asks a lucky employee and learns they both went to the Consul General's office. There are many scattered footprints on the floor, distributed throughout the vault, and of course, also near the shelf where GER.B.11451 belongs.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Of course, we need to see if this size 43 shoe has been here.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Yes, it has.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then David tries not to cover the shoe prints, heads straight for the file, and checks its condition.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Check the dust patterns on the file shelf. Have the files here been disturbed recently?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You easily find file bag GER.B.11451 on the shelf according to the numbering. The seal appears intact.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Looks intact? David carefully examines the seal, trying to find any suspicious traces.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: There's no doubt someone has touched it; not much dust has settled on the document pouch.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Find a suitable spot in the lobby with a direct view of the Consul General's office door, ask a lucky employee for a cigarette to light, pretend to be sneaking a smoke there while actually keeping the office door firmly in my peripheral vision.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew doesn't squeeze into the file rack area; instead, he stands at the door. Hearing that things seem to be finished inside, he asks quietly, "Found it? Everything alright?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Show the document to Gray and have her check it with me.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Ask the guard nearby, "Has anyone else visited the vault today?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: No one answers, so Andrew chooses to go squeeze into the file rack area too.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Study the document pouch carefully together with David.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: What exactly is so good that so many people are crowding around to look? Andrew absolutely has to go see for himself.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Consul General Harvey is harshly reprimanding two subordinates, Jackson doesn't dare breathe loudly beside them, and Brandt has returned to his own office.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: This 1946 document has been handled recently, but this is a confidential mission...

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Continue smoking, patiently waiting for other colleagues to return.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Gray and Johnsen discover that if not examined carefully, the seal looks intact from the outside, but it has actually been opened and subsequently disguised.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David shakes his head at Andrew while signaling him not to make a fuss.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew is very puzzled, but he chooses to follow instructions.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Guard, perhaps you can confirm that this document was in this condition when we just received it." David holds up the document. "Now we need to go upstairs to see Mr. Brandt. Could you please lead the way?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I don't know! I'm only responsible for opening the door, I don't handle the documents."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew takes note of all this.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Don't be nervous, mate." Calm the guard. "You just lock the door properly and help us with directions, that's all."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Mr. Brandt is in the Consul General's office. You can proceed there yourselves. Secretary Jackson's assigned task for me is complete, please understand."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Alright, we'll head over now. Please lock the door."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Pretend to take a stroll to change position, now focusing on Brandt's office door.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player2> wants to discuss something with me privately? Well done, I won't tell anyone the content.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Make sure to watch carefully that the guard has indeed locked the main door securely. David heads towards Brandt's office with the document.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Have the guard point the way and follow him to Brandt's office.
